scope_target.location: items/thm-rank-two-root-system-classification.md:96, Proof step 5.1, claimed reflection images producing intermediate B2/G2 roots
scope_target.evidence: The proof claims alpha1+alpha2, alpha1+2alpha2 and alpha1+3alpha2 are images of alpha1 under s_(alpha2). Its reflection formula gives s_(alpha2)(alpha1)=alpha1-c' alpha2; when (c,c')=(-1,-3), this produces only alpha1+3alpha2. The intermediate roots require the no-gap root-string argument from step 3.2, followed by the displayed reflection producing the remaining G2 root. See Knapp, Proposition 2.48(g) and its proof, printed pp. 153–154: https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~aknapp/download/Beyond2-clickable.pdf. The assigned consumer reaches this supplier through prop-highest-root-exists-and-is-unique-in-an-irreducible-finite-root-system. The root-difference implication consumed here is correctly proved in source step 2.2; the classification statement is not refuted.

evidence.note: Historical 5.1 falsely attributes multiple intermediate roots to one reflection; current owner-repaired proof uses no-gap strings and final G2 reflections.

published_repair_policy.correction: Replace false multiple-image reflection computation by complete no-gap simple-root strings and exact final G2 reflections; close one-sign independence omission; retain Statement and dependencies.
